title: The Old Man and Grandson variant

keywords: the old man and grandson variant
full_text:
An old grandfather lived with his son and daughter-in-law. His eyesight was dim, his hearing was faint, and his hands trembled so violently with age that he often spilled soup upon the tablecloth or dropped his spoon.

Disgusted by the mess, the cold-hearted daughter-in-law made the old grandfather sit in the corner behind the stove, serving his food in a cheap earthenware bowl while the family dined merrily at the main table. The old man sat in silence, tears rolling down his weathered cheeks.

One day, his trembling hands dropped the earthenware bowl, and it shattered upon the flagstones. The woman scolded him bitterly and bought him a rough wooden trough for two farthings, forcing him to eat his meals like a barnyard beast.

A few days later, the parents saw their four-year-old son sitting on the floor, busily carving small pieces of wood with his father's chisel.

"What are you making there, little one?" asked the father fondly.

The little boy looked up with innocent eyes and replied, "I am making a little wooden trough for you and mother to eat out of when you grow old, just like grandfather!"

The parents looked at each other in stunned silence. Overwhelmed by shame and grief, they burst into tears. They walked to the stove, took the old grandfather gently by the hand, led him to the place of honor at the head of the table, and treated him with loving reverence for all the remaining days of his life.
moral: Treat your elders with tenderness and dignity, for your children will follow your example.
